scheme_name: Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank: For Animal Husbandry
description:
The Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank for Animal Husbandry is a significant initiative under the Government of India aimed at promoting animal husbandry in rural areas.

This scheme was launched in 2004 as part of the broader strategy to enhance the livelihoods of rural communities through the development of the livestock sector.

The primary objective of this scheme is to provide financial assistance to farmers and rural entrepreneurs involved in animal husbandry.

The scheme aims to increase the production of milk meat and other animal products by providing necessary financial support.

It also seeks to promote self-sufficiency in animal husbandry and reduce dependency on external sources for livestock products.

The scheme has set a measurable target of increasing milk production by 5 percent annually.

It also aims to enhance the income of rural households by at least 20 percent over five years through improved animal husbandry practices.

The benefits under this scheme include access to credit facilities for purchasing livestock and related equipment.

Farmers can avail loans up to INR 10 lakh for setting up dairy farms or purchasing livestock.

The interest rate on loans provided under this scheme is typically around 7 percent per annum.

In some cases, the government provides interest subsidies to encourage farmers to take loans.

The eligibility criteria for this scheme include being a resident of rural areas and being engaged in animal husbandry activities.

Farmers must be at least 18 years old to apply for the loans under this scheme.

The income limit for eligibility is set at INR 1.5 lakh per annum for individuals and INR 2.5 lakh for families.

Applicants must also possess a valid identification document such as an Aadhaar card or voter ID.

Educational qualifications are not a strict requirement for this scheme.

The application process involves several steps to ensure that the funds reach the intended beneficiaries.

Interested applicants must first approach their nearest Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank branch.

They need to fill out an application form that requests details about their livestock and proposed projects.

Required documents include proof of identity proof address proof and income proof.

Additionally applicants must provide a project report detailing their plans for animal husbandry.

Once the application is submitted it is reviewed by bank officials.

The bank may conduct an on-site inspection to verify the details provided in the application.

If approved the loan amount is disbursed directly to the applicant's bank account.

The disbursement typically occurs within 30 days of loan approval.

The repayment period for loans can range from 3 to 7 years depending on the amount borrowed.

The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers' Welfare.

The National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development also plays a crucial role in funding and supporting this initiative.

Contact details for the implementing authorities can be found on the official Ministry of Agriculture website.

The scheme has seen a steady increase in participation since its inception.

As of 2023 over 1 million farmers have benefited from this scheme.

The total amount disbursed under this scheme has exceeded INR 5,000 crore.

The government has also introduced training programs to educate farmers on modern animal husbandry practices.

These training programs are conducted in collaboration with various agricultural universities and institutions.

The scheme has contributed significantly to rural employment generation.

It has also played a role in improving the nutritional standards of rural households.

The government regularly monitors the progress of the scheme through various performance indicators.

Feedback from beneficiaries is collected to improve the scheme's implementation.

The scheme is part of the larger National Livestock Mission launched in 2014.

The National Livestock Mission aims to enhance livestock productivity and ensure sustainable growth.

Under this mission the government has allocated INR 2,000 crore for various livestock development initiatives.

The Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank for Animal Husbandry is a vital component of this mission.

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The scheme has also been instrumental in promoting cooperative farming practices.

Cooperative societies have been encouraged to participate actively in the implementation of this scheme.

The government has set up a dedicated helpline for farmers to address their queries related to the scheme.

Farmers can call the helpline to get information about the application process and eligibility criteria.

The scheme has received positive feedback from various stakeholders in the agricultural sector.

It has been recognized for its role in empowering rural communities through financial inclusion.

The government continues to promote this scheme through various awareness campaigns.

These campaigns aim to educate farmers about the benefits of animal husbandry and the support available to them.

In conclusion the Primary Cooperative Agriculture and Rural Development Bank for Animal Husbandry is a comprehensive initiative that supports rural livelihoods through animal husbandry.

It provides essential financial assistance and promotes sustainable practices in the livestock sector.

The scheme is a testament to the government's commitment to improving the socio-economic conditions of rural populations in India.
